# FieldSizeTimes — times with the number of runners as denominator

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean · **Diagram:** [The Lonely Runner: pile-ups, shifts and residue sieves](../../GRAPH.md#the-lonely-runner-pile-ups-shifts-and-residue-sieves)

With the number of runners as the denominator, the track is cut into that many equal parts, and one part is exactly the loneliness distance. So at such a time a runner is far enough exactly when it is not at the start (field_size_far_iff), and the runner standing still is lonely exactly when no speed times the numerator is a multiple of the number of runners (field_size_lonely_iff). When the number of runners is prime, the consecutive speeds 1 up to one less than it are lonely at such a time exactly when the numerator is not a multiple of the number of runners (consecutive_prime_field): the tight cases, one runner per fence post. The easy half of Sungkawichai and Trakulthongchai's Remark 3.2, the reason their method needs a prime number of runners. Not proved here: that these are the only lonely times of the consecutive speeds, and their polynomial method over the remainders for a prime (Proposition 4.1).

## Claims

<a id="field_size_far_iff"></a>
### `field_size_far_iff`

With as many parts to the lap as runners, a point is far enough from the start exactly when it is not at the start.

```lean
/-- **One part is the loneliness distance.** With `N` parts to the lap and `N`
runners, a point is far enough from the start exactly when it is not at the
start. -/
def field_size_far_iff : Prop :=
  ∀ (N : ℕ) (y : ℤ), 0 < N → (far N N y ↔ ¬ (N : ℤ) ∣ y)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.FieldSizeTimes.field_size_far_iff_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/FieldSizeTimes.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/FieldSizeTimes.lean)

<a id="field_size_lonely_iff"></a>
### `field_size_lonely_iff`

The runner standing still is lonely at a time with the number of runners as denominator exactly when no speed times the numerator is a multiple of the number of runners.

```lean
/-- **Lonely at a field-size time.** The runner standing still is lonely at the
time `s / (number of runners)` exactly when no speed times `s` is a multiple of
the number of runners. -/
def field_size_lonely_iff : Prop :=
  ∀ (S : Finset ℤ) (s : ℤ),
    lonely_at S (S.card + 1) s ↔ ∀ v ∈ S, ¬ ((S.card + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ v * s
```

**Rests on:** [`FieldSizeTimes.field_size_far_iff`](FieldSizeTimes.md#field_size_far_iff)

**Proof:** `RNS.FieldSizeTimes.field_size_lonely_iff_step` in [`RNSSolutions/FieldSizeTimes.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/FieldSizeTimes.lean)

<a id="consecutive_prime_field"></a>
### `consecutive_prime_field`

If the number of runners is prime, the consecutive speeds are lonely at a numerator over the number of runners exactly when the numerator is not a multiple of it.

```lean
/-- **Consecutive speeds with a prime number of runners.** If `k + 1` is prime,
the speeds `1, …, k` are lonely at the time `s / (k + 1)` exactly when `s` is
not a multiple of `k + 1`. -/
def consecutive_prime_field : Prop :=
  ∀ (k : ℕ), (k + 1).Prime → ∀ s : ℤ,
    lonely_at (Finset.Icc (1 : ℤ) k) (k + 1) s ↔ ¬ ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ s
```

**Rests on:** [`FieldSizeTimes.field_size_lonely_iff`](FieldSizeTimes.md#field_size_lonely_iff)

**Proof:** `RNS.FieldSizeTimes.consecutive_prime_field_step` in [`RNSSolutions/FieldSizeTimes.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/FieldSizeTimes.lean)
